contents:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# /etc/lakebox/setup-home-directory.sh [<username>]
#
# Set up the home directory after attaching the user's persistent volumes.
set -euo pipefail

# Username from the argument, else the PAM session user, else the default user.
USERNAME="${1:-${PAM_USER:-sandbox-agent}}"
HOME_DIR="/home/${USERNAME}"
# Lock on the ephemeral /run tmpfs to serialize concurrent callers.
LOCK="/run/lakebox-home-setup.lock"
# Completion marker (written last, see end of file) recording the current boot.
MARKER="${HOME_DIR}/.home-setup-complete"
BOOT_ID="$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id)"

# Fast path: skip if setup already completed for the current boot.
home_ready() {
  [[ "$(cat "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null)" == "$BOOT_ID" ]]
}
if home_ready; then
  exit 0
fi

# Serialize concurrent callers on the /run lock; fd 9 is held for this process.
mkdir -p /run
exec 9>"$LOCK"
flock 9

# Re-check under the lock: another caller may have finished while we waited.
if home_ready; then
  exit 0
fi

# chown/chmod the (possibly root:root, freshly-mounted) home root FIRST so the
# writes below land under a home the user owns and can write.
chown "${USERNAME}:${USERNAME}" "$HOME_DIR"
chmod 700 "$HOME_DIR"

# Seed the shell config, write-once so a user's later edits are preserved.
if [[ ! -f "${HOME_DIR}/.bashrc" ]]; then
  cp /root/.bashrc "${HOME_DIR}/.bashrc"
  chown "${USERNAME}:${USERNAME}" "${HOME_DIR}/.bashrc"
fi
if [[ ! -f "${HOME_DIR}/.bash_profile" ]]; then
  cat > "${HOME_DIR}/.bash_profile" <<'EOF'
[[ -f ~/.bashrc ]] && . ~/.bashrc
EOF
  chown "${USERNAME}:${USERNAME}" "${HOME_DIR}/.bash_profile"
fi

# The SSH gateway key is served from /etc/ssh/authorized_keys.d/<user> (managed
# by setup-user.sh), so no key is staged under ~/.ssh. Keys a user adds to
# ~/.ssh/authorized_keys still work.

# Credential-config symlinks (~/.databrickscfg, ~/.codex/config.toml,
# ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.databricks/token-cache.json) point at targets under
# /run/lakebox, pre-materialized with valid empty content so the CLIs don't fail
# to parse an empty file before credentials are provisioned.
mkdir -p /run/lakebox
# Create the target only on first run so a provisioned value is never clobbered;
# re-apply ownership every run.
write_placeholder() {
  local target=$1 content=$2
  if [[ ! -e "$target" ]]; then
    printf '%s' "$content" > "$target"
    chmod 600 "$target"
  fi
  chown "${USERNAME}:${USERNAME}" "$target"
}
# (Re)point the symlink at its target, creating the user-owned parent dir.
link() {
  local target=$1 linkpath=$2
  local dir
  dir="$(dirname "$linkpath")"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  chown "${USERNAME}:${USERNAME}" "$dir"
  ln -sfn "$target" "$linkpath"
  chown -h "${USERNAME}:${USERNAME}" "$linkpath"
}
# Empty INI — the databricks CLI appends on login.
write_placeholder /run/lakebox/databrickscfg \
  '; placeholder — populated when credentials are provisioned'$'\n'
link /run/lakebox/databrickscfg "${HOME_DIR}/.databrickscfg"
# Empty token cache.
write_placeholder /run/lakebox/token-cache.json '{"version":1,"tokens":{}}'
link /run/lakebox/token-cache.json "${HOME_DIR}/.databricks/token-cache.json"
# Empty codex config.
write_placeholder /run/lakebox/codex-config.toml \
  '# placeholder — populated when credentials are provisioned'$'\n'
link /run/lakebox/codex-config.toml "${HOME_DIR}/.codex/config.toml"
# Empty Claude Code settings.
write_placeholder /run/lakebox/claude-settings.json '{"env":{}}'
link /run/lakebox/claude-settings.json "${HOME_DIR}/.claude/settings.json"

# Marker written LAST so a run that dies mid-way is retried on the next entry.
printf '%s' "$BOOT_ID" > "$MARKER"
chown "${USERNAME}:${USERNAME}" "$MARKER"
chmod 600 "$MARKER"

echo "home setup complete for ${USERNAME}"
